description: NO-REGRESSION fixture for saga #811 (issue #1087), and it did NOT move: this asserts CORRECT behaviour that had to survive issue #815 unchanged, and its `events`/`diagnostics` are byte-identical to what #1087 recorded. The distinction is normative rather than incidental: `spec/conformance.md:239` makes `challenge`'s canonical signature normative and the arity row at `spec/conformance.md:244` gives it Kind Command with Arity 0, so an excess input is a real error whatever #815 does about the missing evaluator. (`spec/ai-tutor.md` describes `challenge` at length but is marked Status: Informative, stated outright at `spec/conformance.md:236`, so it is not the source of this claim.) It is rejected at PARSE as `ol-bad-token` (stage `parse` per `spec/error-model.md:110`) with `params.text` naming the offending token, so nothing executes and `events` is empty. What #815 had to get right here is the *precedence* rule it introduced: `spec/execution-model.md:768-777` suppresses a token whose ONLY fault is following a callee **nothing resolves**, and bounds that suppression to exactly those — "a resolvable callee is untouched by this rule". `challenge` resolves under a run claiming Tutor, so its stray argument is a genuine finding and survives, exactly as `forward 100 200`'s does. `executeOptions.profiles` is what makes the run claim it; drop it and the same program reports `ol-unknown-command` instead, which is correct for a run that does not claim Tutor and is why the field exists.
